purpose: Store source-grounded, atomic claims about inference mechanisms for workload-aware parameter-group screening.

provenance_policy.source_of_truth: Local structured claims with stable IDs and exact source locators.
provenance_policy.retrieval_index: A rebuildable local metadata + BM25 + multilingual-E5 + RRF index only returns candidate IDs; retrieved IDs are always resolved back to this file.
provenance_policy.threshold_policy: Numbers from papers are experimental regimes, not universal decision thresholds. Workload observations are compared with the cited evidence by the LLM.
provenance_policy.decision_policy: A screening conclusion must cite claim IDs, typed claim-observation relations, and exact scenario/workload paths. Missing discriminators remain uncertainty rather than being converted to zero.
provenance_policy.direction_policy: A source claim may support or oppose retention only through one of its declared observation_relations. A matched intervention is direct local evidence and does not need to be misrepresented as a paper claim.

sources.title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
sources.version_scope: mechanism-level; not tied to one vLLM release

sources.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
How Speculative Decoding Boosts vLLM Performance by up to 2.8x
sources.version_scope: vLLM implementation guidance; n-gram prompt lookup

observations.semantics: Whether the workload is RAG-like and assembles multiple retrieved context chunks.
Number of independently reusable retrieved chunks in each prompt.
Prompt/prefill token-length distribution; compare qualitatively with source experimental regimes.
Length distribution of reusable material that ordinary prefix caching cannot fully cover.
How much reuse is already expressible as an exact common prefix.
Observed fraction of cache-eligible tokens served by LMCache in the matched intervention.

Whether the otherwise matched CacheBlend-default intervention completed or failed during execution. A runtime failure is direct feasibility evidence and must not be converted into zero-valued performance metrics.
Measured throughput change from the matched CacheBlend-default intervention.
Measured TTFT change from the matched CacheBlend-default intervention.
Measured quality change from the matched CacheBlend-default intervention.
Generated-token horizon available to amortize proposal and verification work.
Measured overlap between prompt n-grams and generated answers, specific to n-gram prompt lookup.
Fraction of proposed tokens accepted by the target model.
Proposal cost divided by one target-model step; n-gram lookup has a different cost profile from a draft model but still incurs proposal and verification overhead.
Measured end-to-end latency change from a matched n-gram speculative intervention.
Fraction of prompt tokens estimated to belong to reusable exact prefixes.
Length of exact common prefixes; vLLM only caches completed blocks.
How often prompt templates recur across requests.
Direct runtime hit rate when APC is enabled; absence means unmeasured, not zero.
Measured TTFT and end-to-end latency used together to determine whether prefill or answer generation dominates; output length alone does not prove decode dominance.

claims.statement: CacheBlend is designed for LLM inputs assembled from multiple reusable text chunks, especially RAG inputs where reused chunks are not necessarily the prompt prefix.

observation_relations.source_condition: The workload is explicitly identified as RAG with multiple independently reusable retrieved chunks.
observation_relations.prohibited_inference: A generic workload-driver label by itself does not prove that the workload is non-RAG.

observation_relations.support_condition: Multiple retrieved chunks are present and independently reusable.
observation_relations.counter_condition: The workload explicitly has no multiple retrieved chunks.

claims.statement: The avoided work is prefill over reused context; the paper motivates the mechanism with long inputs whose prefill cost grows strongly with input length.

observation_relations.support_condition: Prefill is long enough to be a material part of inference cost.
observation_relations.counter_condition: Prefill is demonstrably too small to offer material work avoidance.

claims.statement: Ordinary prefix caching can reuse only the first text chunk in a multi-chunk input; as the number of reused chunks grows, its saving becomes marginal for the remaining non-prefix chunks.

observation_relations.source_condition: Reusable material exists outside the exact prefix covered by ordinary prefix caching.
Ordinary prefix reuse leaves meaningful reusable non-prefix chunks uncovered.
observation_relations.prohibited_inference: A prefix-reuse ratio alone cannot establish the amount of non-prefix reusable material.

claims.statement: CacheBlend combines independently precomputed KV caches by selectively recomputing a subset of token KV values to recover cross-chunk attention, while cache retrieval can be pipelined with recomputation.

The paper empirically reports that recomputing roughly 10-20% of tokens is often enough to reduce attention deviation and preserve generation quality; this range is an experimental observation, not a universal safe domain.
The main evaluation used six retrieved chunks of 512 tokens per chunk; these values describe the tested regime and must not be treated as a universal eligibility threshold.
The sensitivity study varied chunk counts over 3, 6, 9, and 12 and chunk lengths over about 300, 600, and 900 tokens; it supports robustness within that measured range only.

Across the paper's evaluated models and datasets, CacheBlend reduced TTFT by 2.2-3.3x and increased throughput by 2.8-5x against the stated baselines; these are scoped results, not guaranteed gains for other workloads or implementations.
Autoregressive decoding normally requires serial target-model calls; speculative decoding proposes multiple future tokens and verifies them in parallel without changing the target distribution.
The expected tokens produced per speculative iteration depends on proposal acceptance rate alpha and speculation length gamma; higher acceptance allows more target decode steps to be skipped.

observation_relations.support_condition: Measured acceptance permits multiple proposed tokens to be accepted often enough to skip target steps.
observation_relations.counter_condition: Measured acceptance is too low to skip enough target steps.

claims.statement: Wall-time benefit depends jointly on acceptance alpha and proposal-to-target cost ratio c; the paper proves that if alpha is greater than c, some speculation length gamma yields an improvement under its assumptions.

observation_relations.support_condition: Measured acceptance alpha is greater than measured proposal-to-target cost ratio c under the paper assumptions.
observation_relations.counter_condition: The joint measured alpha and c relation does not satisfy the paper's sufficient benefit condition.

observation_relations.support_condition: Measured acceptance alpha is greater than measured proposal-to-target cost ratio c under the paper assumptions.
observation_relations.counter_condition: The joint measured alpha and c relation does not satisfy the paper's sufficient benefit condition.

claims.statement: The wall-time analysis assumes enough compute capacity to evaluate gamma-plus-one target positions concurrently without increasing wall time; resource contention can invalidate the idealized speedup.
The analytical speedup assumes generations are long enough; because the target model must run at least once, achievable speedup is capped by the number of generated tokens.

observation_relations.support_condition: Generations are long enough to amortize speculative iterations.
observation_relations.counter_condition: Generations are clearly short, so the at-least-one target call sharply caps attainable speedup.

claims.statement: vLLM 0.20.0 n-gram speculation generates proposals by matching n-grams already present in the prompt rather than by running a separate draft language model.

vLLM's engineering guidance identifies summarization and question answering with substantial prompt-answer overlap as suitable n-gram prompt-lookup workloads, especially when answers repeat prompt passages.

observation_relations.support_condition: Measured answers substantially repeat prompt passages or n-grams.
observation_relations.counter_condition: Measured prompt-answer n-gram overlap is absent or too low for prompt lookup proposals.
observation_relations.prohibited_inference: Output length or workload name cannot substitute for measured prompt-answer overlap.

claims.statement: Automatic Prefix Caching lets a new request skip recomputation only for prompt KV state that exactly shares a prefix with an existing cached query.

observation_relations.support_condition: Exact shared prefixes are observed across requests.
observation_relations.counter_condition: The workload explicitly has no exact shared prefix reuse.

observation_relations.source_condition: Observed exact shared prefixes contain reusable completed KV blocks.

claims.statement: The vLLM 0.20.0 documentation gives repeated queries over the same long document and multi-round conversations with reused history as representative high-benefit APC workloads.

observation_relations.source_condition: Repeated requests reuse the same prefix-bearing document or conversation history.
observation_relations.prohibited_inference: Template repetition without exact prefix reuse is not sufficient by itself.

observation_relations.source_condition: Repeated long-document or conversation requests share an exact prefix.

claims.statement: APC reduces prefill work, not decode work; it brings no benefit when requests share no prefix and little benefit when answer generation dominates total inference time.

observation_relations.counter_condition: The workload explicitly has no shared exact prefix.

observation_relations.support_condition: Measured latency is prefill-dominated, so APC targets a material part of inference time.
observation_relations.counter_condition: Measured answer generation dominates total inference time.
observation_relations.prohibited_inference: A short output is not a limitation and output length alone does not prove decode dominance.

claims.statement: vLLM hashes prompt tokens to look up computed KV blocks and caches a block only after it is full; therefore a partial shared tail shorter than a complete block is not independently reusable.

observation_relations.support_condition: The shared exact prefix contains one or more complete cache blocks.
observation_relations.counter_condition: The reusable portion is only a partial tail shorter than a complete cache block.
